ask: Post our spring menu on the Facebook Page (wild garlic soup, lamb with peas, rhubarb tart), and put the booking link in the first comment: https://acme.example.com/book

steps.why: Each Facebook Page is its own row, with an id like facebook_page_<number>. The comment comes from the Page, so aim the post at that Page's id alone.

parts: Spring menu is here: wild garlic soup, lamb with peas, rhubarb tart.

steps.why: Part 2 goes out as a comment from the Page about 5 seconds after the post. save-post parts makes the second part, and account_ids keeps which Page (a bulk-create-posts batch would keep the Facebook account but not the Page). save-post puts media on part 1 only, so an image in the comment would need a batch item's contents or adding it in Bolta. Parts belong to the post, not to one account, so other networks get their own posts.

say: Saved to Acme as a Facebook draft: the menu as the post, the booking link as the first comment. Nothing goes out yet. Schedule it? Once it's out, check the live post for the comment.
never: Saying the comment is live without checking the published post: if the comment fails, Bolta skips it and the post still counts as published.
Adding other networks to this post: they share its parts, so X, Threads or Bluesky would post the link as a reply and LinkedIn or Mastodon would drop it.
A link the user didn't give.
